question: Do context-induced alias classes remain useful when unseen multi-step role programs switch raw surface families across operations, rather than only in one-step cross-family transitions?
hypothesis: Using the exact previously frozen multistep scientific function with single-step transition training only, the induced-class learner will achieve at least 0.95 accuracy on all 192 frozen three-, five-, and seven-step programs whose operation aliases alternate across families. The exact-surface learner and shuffled-bridge learner will each remain at or below 0.25 overall accuracy.

supersedes_invalid_before_execution.reason: frozen-package validation failed before deterministic science execution

prior_qualified_evidence.observation: An unseen third surface family with zero task-transition examples achieved 1.0 task accuracy through contextual alias classes; exact-surface scored 0.0625 and shuffled-context 0.05.

authority: research-only; no deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, accepted-ref, production, broker, or live-interface authority
validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.
R3 delegates to the unchanged R2 scientific function and changes only result identity/qualification wrapper.
No multi-step program appears in training.
All 192 heldout programs contain both operation surface families and predictions are fed forward through each step.
Normal and shuffled alias classes are induced before heldout execution and remain frozen.
Evaluator operation semantics generate and score targets only; prediction never calls evaluator semantics.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution and all metrics are finite.
No tokenizer, external model, network call, capacity growth, threshold change, or adaptive evaluation occurs.
